subject: Week 52: year one closes — 12-month visit window opens Monday
bodyText:
This week
The full CDC 12-month checklist is now the frame: pulling to stand, cruising, drinking from a held open cup, the thumb-and-finger pickup, block-in-cup play, waving, calling a parent mama or dada, and pausing at no (https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html) — while independent walking and additional words remain emerging for some, each with a 15-month CDC checkpoint. The year-one ledger, quantified: birth weight has typically tripled by 12 months, length is up roughly 50%, and brain volume has nearly doubled — a growth rate he will never repeat. What the evidence said mattered most this year: conversational turns, sleep consolidation, and iron; what mattered least: everything that promised passive gains. Year two's cadence covers the 15-month visit (DTaP #4, expressive-language takeoff), the 18-month M-CHAT autism screen, and preschool tour season opening September 2027.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Stranger wariness and clinging at the birthday gathering — expected at 12 months, not a regression.
- [low concern] A short fussy crash after the first real cake — for many infants this is the first meaningful sugar exposure; it self-resolves.
- [monitor] Multiple absent 12-month milestones — bring the CDC checklist to the well visit rather than waiting for the 15-month one.
- [call within 24h] Vomiting or diarrhea persisting past 24 hours after party food.
- [call now] Severe respiratory distress, blue lips, or unresponsiveness — 911 before anything else.

Enrichment opportunities
- Order the year-1 photo book while the party photos are fresh — 60–100 pages compiled at month 13–14 is the standard build, and the monthly-stack 12-up frame is the other high-yield print.
- Carry the 1000-books cadence into year 2 — one book a day clears 1,000 well before kindergarten, and shared reading remains the highest-evidence enrichment line item in the entire portfolio. 1000 Books Before Kindergarten: https://smcl.org/blogs/post/1000-books-before-kindergarten/
- Hold the daily outdoor walk at 30+ minutes with him doing more of the moving — new walkers rack up dozens of falls an hour while calibrating, and grass or sand is the ideal practice surface. AAP — movement, 8 to 12 months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-8-to-12-Months.aspx
- Confirm the year-2 activity slate in one sitting: music continues, swim starts now that the AAP evidence window opens at age 1, and nothing else needs adding — the marginal class buys logistics, not development. AAP — swim lessons: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/safety-prevention/at-play/Pages/Swim-Lessons.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 364–380 (May 10–26, 2027): 12-month well visit — MMR #1, VAR #1, HepA #1, PCV #4, Hib booster, hemoglobin, lead screen. Mild fever and rash 7–12 days post-MMR is common and not contagious.
- Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first birthday — 60–90 minutes, nap-anchored, cake well-mashed; the day is for the adults and the photo record, and that is fine.
- By Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first dental visit — the AAP by-age-1 marker passes Tuesday; if unbooked, book now.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Shows you an object she likes
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Joint attention with intention to share — distinct from pointing to request. Strong autism-screen marker when consistently absent.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/shows-object-she-likes/complete

- Follows directions given with a gesture and words
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Combined verbal + nonverbal cues. Pure-verbal compliance comes after.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/follows-gesture-plus-words/complete

- Copies other children while playing
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Peer-directed imitation, not just imitation of parents.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/copies-other-children/complete

- Hugs a stuffed doll or other toy
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Pretend nurture — early symbolic play. Often emerges with a favorite lovey.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hugs-stuffed-toy/complete

- Stacks at least two small objects (like blocks)
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Visuomotor coordination + planning. Knocking the stack down is also part of the practice.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/stacks-two-objects/complete
